user.title: Connect to the EZVIZ China Open Platform
user.description: Choose an editable name for this Hub, then enter China Open Platform credentials, not EZVIZ app login credentials. AppKey and AppSecret grant access to your devices: keep them private, never place them in screenshots or issue reports, and review the [official API documentation](https://open.ys7.com/help/19) before selecting polling intervals.

devices.title: Select devices
devices.description: Choose how this hub filters the devices currently returned by the Open Platform. **Include** keeps only the selected devices. **Exclude** keeps every current and future device except those selected. Filtering controls entities, polling, and background event processing; a syntactically valid official webhook envelope is still acknowledged before a filtered or unknown target is ignored.

reconfigure.description: Replace credentials for the same Open Platform application. A different AppKey must be added as a new hub.

init.title: EZVIZ IoT CN options
init.description:
**Near-real-time Cloud Push:** When enabled, EZVIZ can deliver device-native alarm and calling events to this private webhook. Home Assistant immediately returns HTTP 200 with the exact original `messageId`, then parses and deduplicates the event in the background. Keep alarm polling enabled until delivery is verified; polling recovers missed or delayed events and coordinates state after a restart.

**Webhook publishing:** The current URL `{webhook_url}` is sensitive. Use HTTPS and expose only its exact `/api/webhook/...` path; never expose the Home Assistant UI or publish the URL, AppKey, AppSecret, or access token. EZVIZ requires the response within two seconds. An unreachable URL, timeout, or invalid response can trigger retries or degrade Push delivery. Home Assistant shows the new URL in a persistent notification when it is generated for the first time.

**API usage estimate:** {included_device_count} included devices and {capture_channel_count} currently verified capture-capable channels produce an estimated baseline of **{estimated_daily_api_calls} Open Platform API calls/day** plus **{estimated_daily_image_downloads} direct image downloads/day**. The baseline allows two status probes per currently verified light-capable device. It excludes pagination, retries, token refresh, manual refreshes, event-image downloads, device changes, and your application's assigned quota. Shorter intervals increase usage; scheduled capture can consume quota and wake battery-powered devices. Check the [official API documentation](https://open.ys7.com/help/19), [Open Platform Message Push feature development reference](https://open.ys7.com/help/5130), and [Open Platform Console > Cloud Signaling > Message Push](https://open.ys7.com/console/messagePush.html) for authoritative limits and delivery configuration.
